summary: Carlo Formichi (1871–1943) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied under Michele Kerbaker, Georg Bühler, Paul Deussen at Kiel University, and Hermann Oldenberg. He served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (1898) and Sapienza University of Rome (1914–1941).

Carlo Giussani (1840–1900) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1859–1863) and under Giuseppe Bardelli (~1860–1863), Rudolf von Roth (~1863–1864), and Albrecht Weber (1863).
Carlo Jamelle Harris works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA in Philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin (attested 2009).

Carmen Blacker (1924–2009) worked in Japanology and religious studies. She studied at SOAS, Somerville College, under Shigeru Gorai, and at Keio University. She held posts at the University of Cambridge from 1955 and served as president of the Folklore Society (1982–1984).

Carmen Dragonetti (1937–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She studied at the National University of San Marcos and held posts at the Center of Buddhist Studies (~1987–2018), University of Buenos Aires, IIBS (1989), and Nyingma Institute (1996).

Carmen Meinert is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of Bonn (2001) and has held research posts at the University of Hamburg (attested 2008) and Ruhr University Bochum.

Carol Breckenridge (1942–2009) specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–1976) and held a post at the University of Chicago (~1993–1998).

Carol S. Anderson works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under John A. Brinkman and W. S. Karunatillake (1990–1991), and became Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College.

Carola Roloff is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She studied at the University of Hamburg under Geshe Thubten Ngawang and David P. Jackson. Her posts include CIHTS (2006–2007), Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg, and visiting professor at the University of Hamburg (2018–2025).
Carola S. Carstens is an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her doctorate at the University of Hamburg (by 2006) and held a post at Rice University (1998–1999).
Carole M. Cusack is a religious studies scholar. She studied at the University of Sydney from 1988 to 1995 and held a post there in 2013.

Carole McGranahan is a Tibetology and history scholar. Educated at Colgate and the University of Michigan (PhD 2001) under Nicholas Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler, she joined the University of Colorado Boulder, serving as Assistant Professor of Anthropology (~2001–2008).

Caroline Humphrey is a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies and religion. She studied at Cambridge (under Edmund Ronald Leach) and Leeds. Her career includes posts at Girton College, the Scott Polar Research Institute, King's College, and Cambridge university professor (1978–2010).

Caroline Rhys Davids (1857–1942) was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy scholar. She studied at UCL and under T. W. Rhys Davids. She was Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society (1907–1942) and lectured at Manchester (1910–1913) and SOAS (1918–1933).

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt is a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington (attested 1990) and held posts at Ohio State University and Denison University.
Carson T. Schütze is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997. He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1997.

Catherine Bell (1954–2008) was a religious studies and Sinology scholar. She studied at the University of Chicago (~1976–1983) under Joseph Kitagawa and served as Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University (1985–2008).

Catherine Cornille works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at KU Leuven (~1979–1989) and the University of Hawaiʻi (~1983–1984), and served as Associate Professor of Comparative Theology at Boston College (~2004).

Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher (1946–2023) was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. She earned her PhD at the University of Minnesota (~1975–1984) and served there as an Assistant Professor (~1980–2021).

Catherine Ludvik specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She earned her PhD at the University of Toronto (by 2001) under David B. Waterhouse, and held posts at Hanazono University and the Italian School of East Asian Studies.
